title: sentinel-reclaim-and-stratified-model-cascade-for-cross-gpu-oom-resilience
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a sentinel-driven memory reclamation layer plus a stratified model cascade (distil -> quantized -> slim) to prevent and recover from cross-GPU OOMs during continuous batching and heavy KV cache pressure. This ticket covers design, prototype, experiments, and rollout of: (1) GPU-local sentinels that track soft memory watermarks and trigger reclamation; (2) prioritized KV trimming policies with age/score heuristics; (3) cooperative cross-GPU admission control to avoid cascading OOMs; (4) controlled model cascade and retry/backoff paths that degrade fidelity before failing requests; (5) observability and safety gates for canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel agents emit memory-watermark events and can trigger KV trimming or request admission signals.
KV trimming can evict least-value prefixes based on combined (last_access, token_count, score) and is configurable per-runtime.
Cross-GPU admission control prevents >10% request rejection spike during sustained 95th-percentile memory pressure, compared to baseline.
Model cascade path (primary -> quantized -> slim) reduces OOM incidence by >= 65% on the repro load while keeping latency increase within SLO (p95 + 40ms).
Playbook and automated fallbacks exist: retries with backoff, circuit-breaker for hot-models, and clear telemetry to detect regressions.
End-to-end tests and canary run validate correctness; rollout plan documented and approved by runtime leads.
design_notes: Sentinels: per-GPU lightweight process that tracks allocatable vs used memory. Two watermarks: soft (70% by default) -> trigger aggressive KV trimming; hard (92%) -> start cross-GPU admission and model cascade.

KV trimming: maintain metadata (last_access_ts, prefix_token_count, utility_score). Trim strategy is progressive: trim cold prefixes first, then compact largest prefixes; avoid trimming hot prefix to preserve model quality.

Cross-GPU coop: each node publishes current memory_state to a gossip ring. Admission controller uses conservative global headroom estimate to admit or queue requests; uses token-bucket to smooth bursts.

Model cascade: design discrete fallback graph in runtime config: primary_model -> quantized_variant -> slim_variant. Each fallback is associated with SLA upper bounds and quality regression budget. Prefer latency-preserving fallbacks first.
Retries/backoff: exponential with jitter plus immediate retry to cascade variant if admission fails. Bound retries to avoid amplification during cluster-wide pressure.

Trade-offs: aggressive trimming reduces cost but can degrade context quality for long-chat workloads. Cross-GPU coop adds gossip overhead (~1-2% CPU) but prevents cascading failures. Model cascade may introduce semantic drift; must tie to quality checks.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - Lab: implement sentinel + local KV trimming, run deterministic microbenchmarks and mem-replay tests (2 weeks).
Stage 2 - Canary: enable on 5% of runtime with non-critical tenant traffic; monitor mem-watermarks, request rejection, quality delta on probe set (1 week).
Stage 3 - Gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% with kill-switch flags; evaluate cost, p95 latency, and hallucination/regression metrics at each step (2 weeks).
Stage 4 - Global: enable by default with opt-out for pinned-runtime customers; add admin dashboard and alerts for sentinel failures.
checks_and_metrics: OOM rate (per node, per model) - target: reduce by >=65% vs baseline.
KV eviction rate and average prefix age post-eviction.
p95 and p99 latency delta when cascades are triggered.
Quality regressions on probe prompt set (BLEU/EM/Eval rubric) per model variant.
Cross-GPU admission rejections and queue latency.
Canary-specific error budget consumption and rollback triggers.
